library_preparation_preflight.summary: openai-java-core ships only models, builders, and HTTP interfaces — no transport implementation. httpClient() is a required ClientOptions field with no default in this jar; the real implementation lives in the separate openai-java-client-okhttp artifact, which must NOT be pulled in to make live calls since this repo's tests may not reach the real network.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Do not add com.openai:openai-java-client-okhttp and do not attempt to call api.openai.com. ClientOptions.Builder.build() requires httpClient(); supply a small hand-written test implementation of com.openai.core.http.HttpClient returning canned HttpResponse objects (mirroring how tests/src/software.amazon.awssdk/http-client-spi fakes SdkAsyncHttpResponseHandler/SdkHttpContentPublisher in this repo) so the real request-building and Jackson response-parsing pipeline runs end-to-end without any socket. Pass a placeholder key via ClientOptions.builder().apiKey("test-key") directly in code rather than relying on the OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENAI_BASE_URL environment variables, since no live endpoint is available. Most reachability-relevant surface is the Jackson-driven request/response model builders (ChatCompletionCreateParams, etc.) — exercising those via direct serialization round-trips, in addition to the fake-HttpClient path, is the main source of meaningful coverage.
risks: A test generator unfamiliar with the core/transport split may try to construct OpenAIOkHttpClient or call fromEnv(), which doesn't exist in this jar and isn't configured here — leading to a compile failure or an attempted live network call.

jackson-module-kotlin resolves kotlin-reflect transitively for deserializing Kotlin data classes; kotlin-reflect has known friction with GraalVM native-image reflection metadata, which may need extra reachability-metadata entries discovered only once nativeTestCompile/test actually runs.
Local Gradle and Native Image verification remain authoritative — this assessment is based on SDK architecture research, not an actual test run.
